_README: Machine-readable register of STB product-category conventions.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. STB deliberately repurposes POS category codes: the
cleanest available way to split THC out from beer was to book it under a
category the business does not otherwise use. That is a sound operational
decision, but it means the CATEGORY LABEL LIES ABOUT ITS CONTENTS, and a
label that lies is invisible to anyone who was not in the room. On
2026-07-31 it reached an analysis spec written as 'RETAIL_BEER +
RETAIL_CIDER' for a beer-to-go test; running it as written would have
flipped Feb-2025 from -25% to +23% and scored a promo a success on THC
So the convention is recorded HERE, as data a checker can read, rather than
living in someone's memory. check-category-semantics.mjs enforces it.
Adding a convention is how you make an intentional repurposing safe.
Deleting one to silence the gate is how you reintroduce the bug.

THC.description: Hemp-derived THC beverages. A distinct product line, never beer.
THC.not_item_note: Branded merch carrying a THC SKU's name is merch, not THC revenue. 'Tacker' is a tin sign; keep this list ahead of item_patterns or every branded shirt reads as a THC misfile.

CIDER.description: Actual cider. STB has never sold it as a retail/to-go line.
CIDER.note: These three exist only as on-premise cans (Arryved pos_type TR:_ONSITE_CANS). Any RETAIL cider is unexpected and should be investigated, not assumed.

conventions.why: STB sold no cider, so the unused CIDER category was the only available way to split THC out from beer in the POS. A deliberate business convention, not a data error.
conventions.before_that: Zero. THC did not exist as a line before mid-2024, so RETAIL_CIDER reads 0 in every earlier month and enters any 2024-25 comparison as pure growth.
consequences: NEVER sum RETAIL_BEER + RETAIL_CIDER as 'to-go beer'. That is beer + THC.
To-go beer in the Arryved era = item_day pos_type TR:_PKG + TR_SINGLE_TOGO + TR:_CROW/GROWL. Ties to RETAIL_BEER (Dec-2023 $13,794 vs $13,781).
TR:_ONSITE_CANS is on-premise despite being cans, and is where the real ciders live.

conventions.surface: Clover item categories -> CLV_mapCategory_ -> Notion Category select
conventions.why: Same need carried into Clover: THC must be separable from beer. CLV_mapCategory_ tests for thc/cannabis/hemp BEFORE the beer test, so a correctly-named category resolves to THC.
conventions.fragility: The mapper reads the CLOVER CATEGORY NAME, not the item name. A THC item filed under a category whose name lacks a THC token falls through to 'Beer' (if the name contains cider/beer/tap/draft/brew) or to 'Other'. Found live 2026-07-31: 'thc draft 5oz' sits in Other.
consequences: A new THC SKU is only classified correctly if someone files it under a THC-named Clover category.
This gate is the check on that, because nothing in the pipeline validates it.
